sample_unit: machine learning models (ten models across four datasets, two prediction tasks)
models_evaluated: ten machine learning models including three resampling techniques (specific model names not reported in text)

links.outcome: Model responsiveness to synthesized critical or deteriorating patient conditions in mortality prediction
links.effect: Models failed to recognize 66% of synthesized test cases involving injuries; in some instances failed to generate adequate mortality risk scores for all test cases; similar deficiencies in 5-year breast and lung cancer models.
links.quote: For in-hospital mortality prediction, the models tested using our synthesized cases fail to recognize 66% of the test cases involving injuries.

links.outcome: Recognition of severely impaired medical conditions and rapidly deteriorating health by ML models
links.effect: Serious deficiencies in responsiveness: inability to recognize severely impaired conditions or rapid deterioration; 66% of injury cases missed in in-hospital mortality models.
links.quote: We identified serious deficiencies in the models’ responsiveness, i.e., the inability to recognize severely impaired medical conditions or rapidly deteriorating health.

unlisted_practices: Generating synthetic critical-condition test cases to test ML model responsiveness before deployment

screen.reason: Empirical study developing and testing a pre-deployment stress-testing evaluation framework using synthesized critical emergency conditions to detect safety blind spots in risk prediction models.

primary.practice: synthetic stress testing for critical responsiveness prior to deployment
